records.name: Shine Arts Alliance
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts group that helps young artists grow in performing, visual and media arts. Its skate night fundraiser on October 22, 2026 is open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Young artists take part in the group's arts education programs. The public can attend the fundraiser or buy tickets to support the work.

schedule.text: Skate night fundraiser on Thursday, October 22, 2026, 6 to 9 pm. Class days and times are not published on the site.

cost.text: Fundraiser ticket is $20 plus a $0.50 service fee, and includes skate rental and a meal. Class costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the October 22, 2026 skate night on the Shine Arts Alliance site, or call 215-651-4763 to ask about youth arts classes.
first_step.basis: The fundraiser is open to buy, but the site does not explain how to enroll in classes.

records.notes: The mission names performing, visual and media arts. The closest tags were used because the site does not list specific classes. Tuition and class times are not published. The footer copyright (2022 to 2023) and an undated class photo were not counted as evidence. The phone number comes from a link on the site.

records.name: Spanish American Professional Firefighters and EMS Association
records.summary: A Philadelphia association for firefighters and EMS workers that promotes Hispanic and Latino representation in emergency services. It also gives out free smoke detectors, teaches CPR and first aid, and hosts family events for neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors can take part in free smoke detector days, CPR and first aid training, and family events such as the Halloween party. Fire and EMS personnel can join through the membership sign-up page.

schedule.text: Community events through the year. Upcoming: a Halloween party on Sunday, November 1, 2026, a Thanksgiving food drive on Saturday, November 21, and a La Navidad party on Saturday, December 19.

cost.text: Smoke detectors are free. Party tickets are $30 for the Halloween party and $75 for La Navidad. Other costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Join the email list on sapfa911.org to hear about the next smoke detector day, CPR class or family event.
first_step.basis: Community events are open to neighbors, and the site has a clear sign up for event and news emails.

records.notes: The IRS list name is Spanish American Professional Firefighter Association. The www address failed a secure connection check, so the bare domain was read instead. The site calls the group volunteer-run. The Thanksgiving food drive and La Navidad party show no year in the page text, so no year is written for them. No phone or email is published.

records.name: Stick to the Plan Org
records.notes: The website on the IRS list is the group name typed in capitals, not a web address, so no page was found. This group was not searched: both searches went to groups with distinctive names. Nothing could be verified about what the group does. Needs a name search by a later agent.

records.name: Supreme Gospel Entertainment & Marketing
records.notes: The IRS legal name is Supreme Gospel Entertainment & Ministries. The site presents itself as a public relations and music promotion company that serves clients, with no classes, membership or volunteer roles. It mentions youth outreach programs in a donation appeal but describes none, and its donate button has no destination, so it is treated as a business. Two email addresses appear with different spellings of the domain; neither is recorded. Working site with no dated items, so status is probably active. Re-check if the youth programs are described later.

records.name: Talking Tech w/ Wayne
records.summary: A nonprofit that offers free tech help, especially to older adults: a helpline staffed by trained technicians, in-person discussion groups, a newsletter, a TV show and a podcast.
records.what_you_do: Join a discussion group, start one at a church or community center, or sign up for the newsletter. Tech questions can go through the contact form on the site.

cost.text: The helpline is free. Fees for groups or Zoom sessions are not stated.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on ttwwlabs.org, or the Schedule a Call link there, to ask about joining or starting a discussion group.
first_step.basis: Anyone can use the free helpline or sign up for the newsletter, though the site does not say beginners are specifically welcomed.

records.notes: The IRS list name is Talking Tech With Wayne Inc. The Philadelphia link comes from a directory listing found in search and the IRS address, not from the group's own page, which shows no city. talking-tech.org redirects to ttwwlabs.org. The podcast listing (host Wayne Hunter) shows its newest episode dated October 2, 2026, with 160 episodes. An earlier search snippet said June 19, 2026 and 145 episodes, so the listing may have changed; the fetched listing is used. The group's own site mentions podcast episodes, which ties the two together. One transcript names a different speaker, which was not recorded. No phone number or email is published.

records.name: The School Mindfulness Project
records.notes: The legal name is The School Mindfulness Project, Inc. Its program trains whole school communities in Philadelphia public schools. The only dated program item is the 2023 to 2024 academic year, which is more than 24 months old, so status is dormant. Hidden as private because there is no public way in: the program serves school communities, the IRS list website was a typo, and the group has no working website. The domain theschoolmindfulnessproject.org now redirects to schoolmindfulness.org, which is an unrelated spam sales page, so no website is recorded. Re-check if the group gets a working site or a public way to join.

records.name: Triumphant Faith Ministries
records.notes: The website on the IRS list is an email address, not a web address. The email is not recorded because it is not clearly the group's own. No search was left for this group, so no page, service schedule or address was verified. Needs a name search by a later agent.

records.name: United Churches Fellowship
records.notes: The website returned HTTP 403 (access blocked). It was not retried or worked around. The website here is the address the group typed on its tax form, not checked. Nothing else was read, so no summary is written. Needs a later check.

records.name: Why Skip Kindness
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that spreads small acts of kindness through pop-up events, community projects and a scholarship program. It also recruits volunteer Kindness Ambassadors who can help mostly from home.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a Kindness Ambassador, mostly from home, by sharing kindness projects online and suggesting ideas. The group runs its own pop-up events and community projects.

first_step.how: Email whyskipkindness@gmail.com with the subject line 'Volunteer Kindness Ambassador Interest' to ask about the volunteer role.
first_step.basis: Anyone can email to volunteer, and most ambassador duties can be done online.

records.notes: The IRS list name is Why Skip Kindness Inc. The site has no dated news or events, so status is probably active from a working site with no dates. The homepage gives a 2024 501(c)(3) date, which is not an activity date, so no sign of life month is recorded. The IRS address is not used because the site does not publish one. Pop-up dates and scholarship details are not on the site.

records.name: Agape Center for Healing Arts
records.summary: A healing arts group that holds retreats on healing, art and care for the earth. It lists a Philadelphia address and runs an online community on Discord.
records.what_you_do: Attend one of the group's retreats, or join its Discord community through the invite on the website. The site shows retreats in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

schedule.text: Retreats held a few times a year. The most recent dated retreat on the site is July 2025, and no upcoming dates are posted.

first_step.how: Join the Discord community through the invite on agapehealing.center, or email revalexation@gmail.com to ask about the next retreat.
first_step.basis: The retreat sign up process is not described and the cost is not stated, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Agape Center for Healing Arts Inc, and the EIN and address match the site. The most recent retreat on the site is July 2025, more than 12 months ago, so status is probably active. The site also lists retreats in Brazil. The email is the one published on the group's own page.

records.name: All Mentees On Board
records.summary: A Philadelphia youth group that mentors girls through after-school programs, life skills training and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Girls sign up for the A.M.O.B. Girls Work Too program and attend its orientation. Membership for the 2026 to 2027 school year is open through a sign-up form on the site.

schedule.text: After-school programming during the school year, plus a summer program. Office hours are Tuesday to Friday, 10:30 am to 5 pm, and Saturday, 10 am to 2:30 pm.

first_step.how: Fill in the membership form on amobservices.org, or call 267-599-8966 during office hours to ask about the Girls Work Too program.
first_step.basis: Joining takes a sign up or application before you see the program.

records.notes: The legal name is All Mentees On Board Non Profit Organization. The site footer reads 2035, which is a typo and was not used. The age range is not stated, so the crowd is set from the youth focus. A second phone line, 1-866-760-4404 extension 101, is on the site but not recorded. The site lists no social media. Cost is not stated.

records.name: Anointed to Serve Ministries
records.summary: Helps older adults stay safe and independent at home with personal help, connections to services, and protection from exploitation.
records.what_you_do: Older adults or family members can contact the group to ask what help is available. Visitors can also support the group through its sponsor page.

first_step.how: Email Katrina@anointedtoserve.org, or use the contact page on anointed2serve.org, to ask what help is available for an older adult.
first_step.basis: The site does not explain how to enroll or what the help costs, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The IRS list name is Anointed to Serve Ministries Inc Aka Ats. The site also calls it Anointed To Serve Senior Village. The site has no dated items, so probably active comes from a working site with no dates. A staff bio lists a Director of D.C. Operations, so the group may also serve Washington. Philadelphia rests on the IRS address, which is not published on the site and not recorded here. The email domain (anointedtoserve.org) differs from the website domain (anointed2serve.org); both are recorded as published. The closest tag is neighbor_errands, chosen because the site describes concierge style help.

records.name: Asia Adams Save Our Children Foundation
records.notes: The website address returned only a placeholder page with one word, both with and without www, so nothing about the group's work could be read. This group was not searched. The word Foundation may mean a private or family foundation, which is out of scope, so check that before publishing. Needs a later name search.

records.name: Association of Women in Forensic Science
records.summary: A volunteer-run group that supports women in forensic science and offers a Saturday forensic science program for young people, along with school and group workshops.
records.what_you_do: The Club Philly Forensics program meets on Saturdays. Schools and groups can request a workshop by email, at least 30 days ahead.

schedule.text: Club Philly Forensics is a Saturday program. Times and dates are not published on the site, and the site lists no dated events after 2022.

first_step.how: Email info@womeninforensics.org to ask about Club Philly Forensics or to request a workshop.
first_step.basis: The program is described, but the site does not say how a new student or member joins.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Association of Women in Forensic Science Inc. The newest dated item is a past programs list running from 2010 to 2022, so status is dormant. The site also has a live workshop request form and a Saturday program, which could mean it still runs, so a reviewer should check before it goes live. The age range for Club Philly Forensics is given two ways (grades 5 to 12 for the program, ages 12 to 18 for the mobile workshops). No street address, phone or cost is published, and the IRS address is not used. The copyright 2026 footer was not counted as evidence.

records.name: Black Women's Educational Alliance
records.summary: An alliance of Black women in education, founded in 1976, with a Philadelphia chapter. It runs a scholarship fund and is holding its 50th anniversary national convention in November 2026.
records.what_you_do: Members pay dues to join the alliance. Anyone can register for the November 2026 convention, which includes a keynote, workshops and a vendor marketplace.

schedule.text: The 50th anniversary national convention, Rooted and Rising, on Friday and Saturday, November 6 and 7, 2026.

locations.label: Crowne Plaza, King of Prussia, PA (convention venue)

first_step.how: Register for the November 6 and 7, 2026 convention through the Register Now link on bweaphilachpt.org, or email bweaphilachpt@gmail.com to ask about membership.
first_step.basis: Membership needs dues and the steps are not explained, though convention registration is open on the site.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Black Womens Educational Alliance Incorporated. The site title reads BWEA Philadelphia, and the contact page gives a Philadelphia P.O. Box (27074, 19118), so the Philadelphia chapter is supported by the group's own pages. The convention is in King of Prussia, outside the city. The last sign of life is the convention month announced on the homepage, since the page has no publication date. Convention and dues prices are not stated. Presenter contact details on the page were not recorded because they are not BWEA's.

blocked.note: HTTP 403 on fetch. Not retried and not worked around.

notes: Used 2 of 2 WebSearch calls, both on groups with distinctive names (The School Mindfulness Project and Talking Tech w/ Wayne), so the search budget is spent. Used 23 fetches, including one secure connection failure (www.sapfa911.org, recovered with the bare domain), one 403 (United Churches Fellowship), two redirects and one spam page. Four groups had no usable web address (Stick to the Plan Org, Triumphant Faith Ministries, Talking Tech and The School Mindfulness Project; the last two were resolved by search). Stick to the Plan Org and Triumphant Faith Ministries had no search left, so they stay unknown with no summary and will be held back. United Churches Fellowship is blocked and Asia Adams Save Our Children Foundation shows only a placeholder, so both are unknown too. Addresses from the IRS list were not used anywhere, because some look like homes; only addresses a group publishes on its own site are recorded. schoolmindfulness.org now serves an unrelated spam sales page and was not used as a source. A separate Philadelphia school mindfulness group, Mindfulness Through Movement Inc, was named in search results but not checked, and no URL was recorded for it. Supreme Gospel Entertainment & Marketing is a marketing business with no community program described, so it is not_a_group.
